findings.text: Ana Brindle assigned all IP in Wickhatch to the company on incorporation; the deed is signed and dated.
Two outside contributors committed to Wickhatch in 2025 before the CLA policy existed. Apache-2.0 still grants the rights the company needs; written confirmations would close the point.
Wickhatch is Apache-2.0 with a correct NOTICE file. The hosted service uses two LGPL-2.1 libraries, dynamically linked: acceptable.
10,000 of the 40,000 granted options have no board resolution approving the grant.
findings.resolved: Ratified by written resolution on 1 November (answer to q4). Now green.

findings.text: Joss Merrow has a pre-emption right on any transfer of founder shares. A sale of existing shares to Kestrel Row needs a waiver.
All five staff contracts carry IP and confidentiality clauses; notice periods of one to three months.
The data processing agreement covers one US sub-processor with older transfer wording; it should use the UK International Data Transfer Addendum.
Records of processing are current; the impact assessment covers the hosted scanner, which reads customer code but stores only findings.
Accounts reconcile to the bank. Monthly burn £58,000; runway nine months before the round.
38 paying teams; annual recurring revenue £312,000, with no customer above 9% of it.
One low-severity incident in 2026, logged, disclosed to the two affected customers and closed in 2 days.
Added after v2: the £300,000 founder loan to the company needs written terms (interest, ranking, repayment).
findings.resolved: Loan terms supplied 4 November (answer to q12): interest-free, behind trade creditors, repayable on a sale or by board decision after 36 months.

questions.q: Does the cap table reconcile with the register of members, share by share?
questions.a: Yes. 1,000,000 shares: Ana Brindle 880,000, Joss Merrow 20,000, option pool 100,000 reserved (40,000 granted). Register and cap table match.

questions.q: Is any dependency of Wickhatch under a licence that conflicts with Apache-2.0?
questions.a: No. The scan lists 212 dependencies: MIT, BSD and Apache-2.0. Two LGPL-2.1 libraries are used by the hosted service only.

questions.q: Which sub-processors handle customer data, and where?
questions.a: Three: hosting in London, email in Dublin, error tracking in the US (the transfer wording finding f7).

questions.q: Which board resolution approved each option grant?
questions.a: 30,000 by resolutions of March and June 2026. The other 10,000 were ratified by written resolution on 1 November; copy added to the data room.

questions.q: What is the monthly burn and how does the budget use the round?
questions.a: Burn £58,000 a month. The budget adds four engineers and one sales hire over 18 months.

questions.q: What share of revenue comes from the largest customer?
questions.a: 8.6% of annual recurring revenue; no customer above 9%.

questions.q: Will the two pre-policy contributors confirm their contributions in writing?
questions.a: One has confirmed; the second has agreed and will sign this month. Both contributions are under Apache-2.0 either way.

questions.q: Has any customer data been exposed in an incident?
questions.a: No. The one 2026 incident exposed scan metadata of two customers for 40 minutes; no secrets or code.

questions.q: Do any staff hold rights to code written before they joined?
questions.a: No. Each contract lists prior inventions; all five lists are empty.

questions.q: Has the board approved the hosted service terms?
Will Joss Merrow waive pre-emption on the sale of existing founder shares?
questions.a: Yes. Waiver signed by Joss Merrow on 4 November; filed in the data room.

questions.q: On what terms does Ana Brindle lend £300,000 to the company?
questions.a: Interest-free, ranking behind trade creditors, repayable on a sale or by board decision after 36 months.

positions.reason: At a seed stage the founder drives the company. Kestrel Row keeps a board seat, an approved list for the independent, and nine consent matters.
positions.moves: Moves governance risk to Kestrel Row; offset by the consent matters and information rights.

positions.reason: First read: an open-ended put option at the round price could fall due at the worst time for the fund. Moved to negotiate once limited to loss of board control and a time window (12 months in v4).
positions.moves: Puts a contingent liability on Kestrel Row; capped by the trigger and the 12-month window.

positions.reason: Kestrel Row pays £4.80 a share either way (249,999 shares, rounded down, against 250,000 in v1) and owns more of the company (21.82% against 20.00%). The company gets £700,000 of equity and a £300,000 founder loan.
positions.moves: Less cash in the company than v1 (£1.0m against £1.2m); more ownership for Kestrel Row.

positions.reason: Kestrel Row asked for participation capped at 3x in v3. Accepted 1x non-participating (u2) in return for broad-based anti-dilution and the board approval list.
positions.moves: Less downside protection on a modest sale; little effect on a large one.

positions.reason: The value is in the hosted service and the community around Wickhatch. A closed relicence would harm both.
positions.moves: No change: the hosted service is what Kestrel Row is buying into.

positions.reason: Kestrel Row can give warranties of capacity, authority and its own information, and quarterly information both ways. It cannot warrant the business, so the mirror is limited to what an investor knows.
positions.moves: A small new exposure for the fund; the founder indemnity cap falls from 2x to 1x the amount invested.

positions.reason: The plain versions make the IC memo faster to write and easier for the partners to read.
positions.moves: If plain and legal wording differ, the plain intent wins: a reason to review both.

positions.reason: Kestrel Row wants the same discipline: no clause may quietly undo an agreed point.
positions.moves: Lowers drafting risk for both sides; it caught clause 7.2 in v3.

children.text: Wickhatch stays open source under Apache-2.0, and nobody can make the company close it.

children.label: Português (Portugal)
children.text: O Wickhatch continua em código aberto, sob a licença Apache-2.0, e ninguém pode obrigar a empresa a fechá-lo.

children.label: mirror
children.text: Every obligation on the founder is asked of the investor too: information, warranties, notice periods.

children.label: Warranties and indemnity
children.text: Warranties from both sides; the founder indemnity capped at the amount invested; the investor warrants capacity, authority and its own information.

children.label: Clause 7.2: Limit of the founder indemnity
children.text: The aggregate liability of the Founder under the Warranties and the indemnity in clause 7.1 shall not exceed the amount invested. The Investor gives the warranties in Schedule 5 as to its capacity, its authority and the information it has supplied.

children.label: Plain English
children.text: If Ana Brindle's statements about the company prove wrong, Ana Brindle owes no more than the £1.2m invested; Kestrel Row also stands behind what it has said about itself.

children.label: Português (Portugal)
children.text: Se as declarações da Ana Brindle sobre a empresa se revelarem incorretas, a sua responsabilidade fica limitada ao montante investido, 1,2 milhões de libras, e a Kestrel Row também responde pelo que declarou sobre si própria.

children.label: Costs
children.text: Each side pays its own desk; shared deal-room tasks are split equally (clause 14.1).

children.label: Clause 14.1: Costs
children.text: Each party shall bear its own costs. The cost of tasks run in the shared deal room shall be borne equally by the Company and the Investor.

children.label: Plain English
children.text: Each side pays for its own team; jobs done together in the deal room are paid half each.

children.label: Português (Portugal)
children.text: Cada parte paga a sua própria equipa; as tarefas feitas em conjunto na sala de negociação são pagas a meias.

children.label: Information rights
children.text: Both ways: monthly accounts to the investor; the investor reports material conflicts and follow-on intentions to the company each quarter.

children.label: plain-terms
children.text: Every clause has a plain-language version; if they differ, the plain version states the intent.

children.label: no-surprises
children.text: Every understanding confirmed in writing is binding on the drafting: a clause that contradicts one is void until both sign again.

memo.title: Investment committee memo: Brindlewood Security, seed
memo.recommendation: Invest £1,200,000 in Brindlewood Security on the v4 terms: 249,999 shares at £4.80, 21.82% of the company after the round.
sections: Brindlewood Security makes Wickhatch, an open-source secrets scanner under Apache-2.0, and sells a hosted service to teams. Six people. 38 paying teams, annual recurring revenue £312,000, monthly burn £58,000.

£700,000 buys 145,833 new shares and £500,000 buys 104,166 existing shares from Ana Brindle, all at £4.80 and rounded down to whole shares. Ana Brindle lends £300,000 of the sale proceeds to the company, interest-free. The company receives £1,000,000 in all; Kestrel Row holds 249,999 of 1,145,833 shares (21.82%), against 20.00% under our v1.

Ana Brindle keeps 775,834 shares (67.71%) and the board majority. Kestrel Row has one director, approves the list for the independent, and has 9 consent matters. If Ana Brindle loses the board majority, Ana Brindle may sell at £4.80 within 12 months: a contingent call on the fund of up to £3.72m, which only arises if Kestrel Row and the independent act together against the founder.

1x non-participating preference; broad-based weighted average anti-dilution; 25% of founder shares re-vest over two years; founder indemnity capped at £1,200,000; Kestrel Row warrants its capacity, authority and own information.

14 documents read, 12 findings: 7 green, 4 amber, 1 red. The red (10,000 options without a resolution) was ratified on 1 November. Ambers: contributor confirmations, the angel waiver (signed), the US transfer wording, the founder loan terms (supplied).

Ana Brindle published eight principles before we looked. We accepted five as written, negotiated the preference, the mirror and the exit right, and all eight are in v4. Every clause has a plain version in English and Portuguese.

Revenue concentration is low; the main risk is execution on the hosted service. Less cash enters the company than in v1, offset by the founder loan. The exit right is the one new kind of obligation for the fund.

First look on 31 October, our v1 term sheet 44 hours later, v4 agreed on 7 November. The Consistency agent stopped v3, which still capped the indemnity at twice the amount invested after both counsels had signed u1.

principles.text: The founder keeps control of direction: a majority of votes on the board and of ordinary shares until a sale or listing.

Investors may buy existing founder shares instead of new ones, with the founder lending the company what it needs.

sections.heading: The round
sections.body: £700,000 buys 145,833 new shares and £500,000 buys 104,166 existing shares from Ana Brindle, all at £4.80 and rounded down to whole shares. Ana Brindle lends £300,000 of the sale proceeds to the company, interest-free. The company receives £1,000,000 in all; Kestrel Row holds 249,999 of 1,145,833 shares (21.82%), against 20.00% under our v1.

sections.heading: Control
sections.body: Ana Brindle keeps 775,834 shares (67.71%) and the board majority. Kestrel Row has one director, approves the list for the independent, and has 9 consent matters. If Ana Brindle loses the board majority, Ana Brindle may sell at £4.80 within 12 months: a contingent call on the fund of up to £3.72m, which only arises if Kestrel Row and the independent act together against the founder.

sections.heading: Protection
sections.body: 1x non-participating preference; broad-based weighted average anti-dilution; 25% of founder shares re-vest over two years; founder indemnity capped at £1,200,000; Kestrel Row warrants its capacity, authority and own information.

sections.heading: Diligence
sections.body: 14 documents read, 12 findings: 7 green, 4 amber, 1 red. The red (10,000 options without a resolution) was ratified on 1 November. Ambers: contributor confirmations, the angel waiver (signed), the US transfer wording, the founder loan terms (supplied).

sections.heading: Principles
sections.body: Ana Brindle published eight principles before we looked. We accepted five as written, negotiated the preference, the mirror and the exit right, and all eight are in v4. Every clause has a plain version in English and Portuguese.

sections.heading: Risks
sections.body: Revenue concentration is low; the main risk is execution on the hosted service. Less cash enters the company than in v1, offset by the founder loan. The exit right is the one new kind of obligation for the fund.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body: First look on 31 October, our v1 term sheet 44 hours later, v4 agreed on 7 November. The Consistency agent stopped v3, which still capped the indemnity at twice the amount invested after both counsels had signed u1.
